items.title: Call to Order
notes: Mayor Watters welcomed everyone and called the meeting to order.

items.title: Land Acknowledgement
notes: Councillor Adams read the Land Acknowledgement.

items.title: Addendums and Corrections to the Agenda
notes: K. O’Kane indicated a correction was made to the June 10th minutes that was inadvertently missed when the file was uploaded to iCompass.

items.title: Disclosure of Pecuniary Interest Under the Municipal Conflict of Interest
notes: Act

Mayor Watters declared a conflict of pecuniary interest with respect to agenda item 8.6, Elora Centre for the Arts – Request for Interest Free Loan as Riverfest has an office in the Elora Centre for the Arts building.

items.title: Introduction of Artist - Steven Jones
notes: Barb Lee, Elora Arts Council introduced Steven Jones as the local artist currently displaying his art in the Council Chamber.
Steven Jones noted his experience painting water colour landscapes and his passion for capturing nature.

items.title: Mayor's County Council Report
notes: Mayor Watters and Councillor Lustgarten Evoy provided highlights of the Multicultural festival held this past weekend at the Wellington County Museum.

items.title: Councillor's Committee Updates
notes: Councillor MacDonald noted a luncheon held at the Senior Centre sponsored by safety communities and Councillor Adams provided highlights of the Groves Hospital Annual General Meeting.

items.title: Susan Fielding and Robert Pasuta re: 8.3 Private Underground
notes: Infrastructure in Road Allowances

Robert Pasuta, farmer and former Municipal Councillor and Susan Fielding, former Councillor in Puslinch appeared in support of the staff report and expressed their appreciation for staff’s agreement to move forward with the request from Sloping Acres through an Encroachment Agreement.

items.title: Consent Items
notes: Consent Agenda Items are considered routine in nature and are voted on collectively. However, any Member of Council may request one or more items be removed from the Consent Agenda for separate discussion and/or action.
Councillor MacDonald noted she attended the Heritage Centre Wellington Committee meeting and toured the home and feels the property is deserving of designation.

items.title: Approval and Receipt of Minutes
notes: THAT the minutes of the Council Meeting held June 10, 2024 be approved as circulated;
AND THAT the Heritage Centre Wellington Minutes be received for information.

items.title: Canada Community-Building Municipal Funding Agreement and
notes: Housing Needs Assessment
Report from A. McNabb, Managing Director of Corporate Services & Treasurer

A. McNabb, Managing Director of Corporate Services & Treasurer provided an overview of the report, indicating the agreement previously executed in 2014 is now up for renewal. He responded to questions regarding details of the work previously undertaken, examples of the synergies and cost savings to be achieved, and the establishment of a new capital account for the Housing Needs Analysis is required by March 2025.

items.title: Elora Green Space Lighting
notes: Report from P. Newson, Managing Director of Community Services P. Newson, Managing Director of Community Services provided an overview of the report, including adding to the recommendation the ability to control the times of operation. Staff responded to questions regarding the impact of the lighting, value of the investment, authority to adjust the plan and lighting, consultation with the Elora BIA, staff resources and the procurement process related to donations.

items.title: Indigenous-themed Sports Logos in Township Facilities Update
notes: Report from P. Newson, Managing Director of Community Services P. Newson, Managing Director of Community Services provided an overview of the report and responded to questions regarding the timeline and budget impact.

items.title: Belwood Child Care and Recreation Feasibility Report
notes: Report from D. Wilson, Chief Administrative Officer

D. Wilson, Chief Administrative Officer provided an overview of the report, including the child care shortfalls, discussions with possible community partners, child care in Belwood, and the recommended approach and next steps.
Councillor Wilton expressed an interest in encouraging County Council to establish more child care facilities.
Mayor Watters called for a recess to confer with staff, the meeting resumed at 3:41 pm.
Mayor Watters indicated Councillor Wilton’s suggestion has been included in the staff recommendation for Council’s consideration.

motions.item_title: Indigenous-themed Sports Logos in Township Facilities Update
motions.text: THAT the Council of the Township of Centre Wellington receive report CS2024-22 Indigenous-themed Sports Logos in Township Facilities Update for information purposes; AND THAT Council directs staff to reinstall the banners at the Jefferson Elora Community Centre arena, exclusive of banners displaying indigenous themed logos or names, until such time as Council has implemented a policy on Indigenous-themed Sports Logos in Township Facilities; AND THAT Council directs staff to continue the work with the Indigenous-themed Sports Logos in Township Facilities Working Group under the DEI Advisory Committee, to develop that policy, and that progress on that initiative be shared with the community on the Connect CW website at www.connectcw.ca.

motions.item_title: Belwood Child Care and Recreation Feasibility Report
motions.text: THAT the Council of the Township of Centre Wellington receives report CAO2024-11 for information; AND THAT the Council of the Township of Centre Wellington supports a collaborative approach to child care planning, funding, administration, and operations lead by Wellington County with the Township playing a supportive role as outlined in this report; AND THAT this report and approved recommendations be forwarded to Wellington County Council and relevant staff for their information to stress the importance of the County’s ongoing leadership and involvement in providing child care services in Centre Wellington, as well as the Township’s offer of support; AND THAT Council defer decisions on future outdoor recreation needs in Belwood until the completion of the ongoing Parks and Recreation Plan, which will provide a comprehensive assessment of the needs in Centre Wellington. AND THAT Council directs staff to send a letter to the County of Wellington encouraging County Council to consider investigating building child care facilities.
motions.text_html: THAT the Council of the Township of Centre Wellington receives report CAO2024-11 for information; AND THAT the Council of the Township of Centre Wellington supports a collaborative approach to child care planning, funding, administration, and operations lead by Wellington County with the Township playing a supportive role as outlined in this report; AND THAT this report and approved recommendations be forwarded to Wellington County Council and relevant staff for their information to stress the importance of the County’s ongoing leadership and involvement in providing child care services in Centre Wellington, as well as the Township’s offer of support; AND THAT Council defer decisions on future outdoor recreation needs in Belwood until the completion of the ongoing Parks and Recreation Plan, which will provide a comprehensive assessment of the needs in Centre Wellington. AND THAT Council directs staff to send a letter to the County of Wellington encouraging County Council to consider investigating building child care facilities.
